evidence.quote: Winding along the Lake Wales Ridge, SR 17 provides scenic vistas and access to lakes, natural areas, citrus agricultural fields

evidence.claim: SR 17 winds through the hills of the Lake Wales Ridge, linking lakes, citrus fields and historic town centers.
evidence.quote: SR 17, or Scenic Highway as it is locally known, serves the historic centers of these communities

evidence.claim: The Ridge Scenic Highway extends 38.7 miles between Haines City and US 27 south of Frostproof.
evidence.quote: extends 38.7 miles along the Lake Wales Ridge, from its intersection with US 27 south of Frostproof to its intersection with US 17/92 in Haines City.

evidence.claim: Designated in 2005, the byway is presented by Florida Scenic Highways as a journey through rural agricultural Central Florida, with access to lakes and natural areas.
evidence.quote: Designated: February 16, 2005

evidence.claim: the byway is presented by Florida Scenic Highways as a journey through rural agricultural Central Florida, with access to lakes and natural areas.
evidence.quote: Enjoy the sight of the historic communities and rural agricultural areas for which Central Florida is famous. Winding along the Lake Wales Ridge, the byway offers scenic vistas and access to lakes, natural areas, citrus agricultural fields

evidence.claim: The ridge itself preserves remnants of ancient sand islands, with white sand visible in neighborhoods built along it. Its landscape includes scrub, flatwoods, wetlands and lakes.
evidence.quote: It is the remnants of those islands that make up today's Lake Wales Ridge.

evidence.claim: with white sand visible in neighborhoods built along it
evidence.quote: Today several communities are located inside the Lake Wales sand ridge, with the white sands visible in many neighborhoods.

evidence.claim: Its landscape includes scrub, flatwoods, wetlands and lakes.
evidence.quote: The area's landscape includes scrub, flatwoods, wetlands, and lakes.

evidence.claim: The road acquired its SR 17 number in the statewide renumbering of 1945.
evidence.quote: State Road 17 was first designated in 1945 after a statewide renumbering of state roads.

evidence.claim: When US 27 was extended south to Miami in 1948, much of its planned alignment between Haines City and Sebring had yet to be built.
evidence.quote: US 27 was extended from Tallahassee south to Miami in 1948, though much of its planned route along SR 25 between Haines City and Sebring had not yet been built at that point.

evidence.claim: Much of SR 17 therefore carried the temporary US 27 designation until the new alignment was completed in the late 1950s.
evidence.quote: As a result, much of SR 17 was designated as "Temporary US 27" until the current alignment of US 27 was completed in the late 1950s.

evidence.claim: Parts then became US 27 Alternate; that designation was removed between the Frostproof area and Haines City in 1998.
evidence.quote: After the completion of US 27, parts of SR 17 were designated as "US 27 Alternate", though this designation has since been removed in 1979 between Sebring and Avon Park and between the Frostproof area and Haines City 1998.

evidence.claim: Traveling south from Haines City, the corridor passes Lake Hamilton and Dundee before reaching Lake Wales, with Bok Tower Gardens north of downtown.
evidence.quote: Frostproof, Hillcrest Heights, Babson Park, the Village of Highland Park, Lake Wales, Lake of the Hills, Dundee, Lake Hamilton and Haines City.

evidence.claim: with Bok Tower Gardens north of downtown
evidence.quote: north of downtown Lake Wales passes by Bok Tower Gardens.

evidence.claim: Continue through Babson Park and Hillcrest Heights to Frostproof, then to the junction with US 27.
evidence.quote: A longer section runs from US 27/98 in Polk County, southwest of Frostproof. It bisects that town, taking the name "Scenic Highway" as it winds through Hillcrest Heights and Babson Park

evidence.claim: Bok Tower began with a practical job as well as a musical one.
evidence.quote: By 1925, Bok had decided to replace the bird sanctuary's water tower with a stone water-and-bell tower.

evidence.claim: By 1925, Edward Bok had decided to replace his bird sanctuary’s water tower with a stone tower holding both water and bells.
evidence.quote: By 1925, Bok had decided to replace the bird sanctuary's water tower with a stone water-and-bell tower.

evidence.claim: The 60-bell carillon occupies the top, while tanks elsewhere in the structure supplied irrigation for the gardens.
evidence.quote: The 60-bell carillon occupies only the top of the Singing Tower, some of the rest contained large water tanks to irrigate the gardens

evidence.claim: Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. had been commissioned to transform the dry sandhill; trenches, pipes and imported soil preceded the planting.
evidence.quote: The first year was spent digging trenches and laying pipes for irrigation, after which soil was brought to the site by thousands of truck loads and plantings began.

evidence.claim: Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. had been commissioned to transform the dry sandhill
evidence.quote: They commissioned landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. to transform what then was an arid sandhill

evidence.claim: The 205-foot tower combines pink and gray marble with coquina stone, and its architectural sculpture depicts Florida plants and animals.
evidence.quote: It is built of pink Etowah marble and gray Creole marble, mined in Tate, Georgia, and coquina stone from St. Augustine, Florida.

evidence.claim: The 205-foot tower
evidence.quote: The 205-foot (62 m) Singing Tower

evidence.claim: its architectural sculpture depicts Florida plants and animals
evidence.quote: the Art Deco architectural sculpture was designed and executed by Lee Lawrie, and depicts Florida flora and fauna

evidence.claim: At Spook Hill in Lake Wales, cars appear to roll uphill: the attraction is an optical illusion known as a gravity hill.
evidence.quote: Spook Hill is a gravity hill, an optical illusion in Lake Wales, Florida, where cars appear to roll up the spooky hill.

evidence.claim: Its setting is the Lake Wales Ridge, a range of sand and limestone hills that formed islands when sea levels were higher two to three million years ago.
evidence.quote: Spook Hill is located on the Lake Wales Ridge, a geologically significant range of sand and limestone hills, which were islands from two to three million years ago, when sea levels were much higher than at present.

evidence.claim: The attraction stands beside Spook Hill Elementary School, which adopted Casper the Friendly Ghost as its mascot.
evidence.quote: The attraction is adjacent to Spook Hill Elementary School, which adopted Casper the Friendly Ghost as their school mascot.

evidence.claim: In 2019, Spook Hill joined the National Register of Historic Places.
evidence.quote: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2019.

evidence.claim: The name Frostproof was chosen to persuade prospective landowners that frost would never destroy the community’s citrus economy.
evidence.quote: The name was a marketing ploy to convince potential landowners that the community has never had, and never would have, a frost that could destroy the large citrus-driven economy.

evidence.claim: Then the Great Freeze of 1894 and 1895 killed most of the citrus here.
evidence.quote: a frost during the Great Freeze winter of 1894 and 1895 killed most of the citrus in Frostproof.

evidence.claim: The town lies between Lake Clinch and Lake Reedy, with its historic downtown district running along Wall Street between the two lakes.
evidence.quote: Its historic downtown district runs east and west between Lake Clinch and Lake Reedy on Wall Street.

evidence.claim: The community incorporated as a town in 1918 and became the City of Frostproof in 1960.
evidence.quote: The Town of Frostproof was incorporated as a municipality on June 18, 1918, and was approved by the Florida Legislature the following year. It officially became the City of Frostproof on November 11, 1960.

evidence.claim: Rail service arrived in 1912; the historic Atlantic Coast Line depot dates from that year.
evidence.quote: After many delays, Frostproof first received rail service in 1912.

evidence.claim: the historic Atlantic Coast Line depot dates from that year
evidence.quote: The Historic Atlantic Coast Line Train Depot, built in 1912

evidence.claim: The Ramon Theater, built in 1925, continues to host live entertainment.
evidence.quote: Frostproof is also home to the Historic Ramon Theater built in 1925. The theater is still in operation and hosts live music and entertainment
